exposure: placental location next to or in the scar niche
Grade 1 (intermediate suspicion) if the placenta is next to or on the scar
transvaginal ultrasound in the early prediction of placenta accreta spectrum
Grade 0 (no suspicion) if the placenta is not next to the scar
Grade 2 (high suspicion) if the placenta was inside the scar niche
Sonographic signs of placenta accreta spectrum
cohort: Women with a history of cesarean delivery who had transvaginal ultrasound at 11 to 14 weeks' gestation between September 2016 and May 2018
finding: Transvaginal ultrasound between 11 and 14 weeks' gestation in women with a prior cesarean delivery can identify at least 3 of 4 cases of placenta accreta spectrum.
